title: Ask the Right Question
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Match six result claims to the question that best exposes the weakness in each.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify six result claims by the question that best exposes the weakness in each, correctly matching at least five of six on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The six questions for evaluating result claims, from the section "Evaluating Result Claims" in Chapter 23, and Chapters 2 and 3.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classify one item at a time with immediate feedback; first-attempt scoring
keyQuestions: What is missing from the claim?
commonMisconceptions: Any claim with a number is evidence.
One question is enough for every claim.
A strong result needs no questions.
assessmentOpportunities: "94 percent of teachers said they love the program." Which question exposes it?
Is any claim with a number evidence?
"A new preprint shows an AI tutor doubles learning." Which question?

controls.name: Category buttons
controls.description: Choose the question for the current claim.

controls.name: Submit
controls.description: Checks the choice. Two tries per claim; only the first counts.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: Moves to the next claim. Finish shows the score.

controls.name: Start over
controls.description: Reshuffles and begins a new run.
